title: Medi-Cal Essential Health Benefits
text: Lists medically necessary Medi-Cal benefits, including dialysis, organ transplants, and maternity care.

title: Medi-Cal End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD)
text: Guidance for people with end-stage renal disease who have Medi-Cal, including how to apply for Medicare.

title: Medicare ESRD eligibility and coverage
text: Explains Medicare eligibility for people with end-stage renal disease, when coverage starts and ends, coordination with employer coverage, and drug coverage after a transplant.

title: Medicare dialysis services and supplies
text: Details Medicare Part A and Part B coverage for dialysis, including facility and home dialysis services, and what members pay.

title: Medicare kidney transplant coverage
text: Describes Medicare coverage for transplant care, donor services, and immunosuppressive drugs, and advises checking Medicare Advantage networks and authorization rules.

title: Medicare Coverage of Kidney Dialysis & Kidney Transplant Services
text: Detailed Medicare guide to covered services, costs, and limits for kidney dialysis and kidney transplants.

title: CMS ESRD Prospective Payment System
text: Explains Medicare's payment policy to providers for dialysis services, supplies, and related care. Mainly useful for understanding what a dialysis facility's payment covers.

title: Medi-Cal All Plan Letter 26-005: Maternity Services
text: Managed-care guidance on maternity benefits. Defines the postpartum period as up to 12 months after pregnancy, including after miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion.

title: Medi-Cal Maternal and Perinatal Health Care Services
text: Member overview of Medi-Cal pregnancy and postpartum care, miscarriage and abortion care, prescriptions, hospital care, doulas, and family planning.

title: Presumptive Eligibility for Pregnant People (PE4PP)
text: Immediate, temporary Medi-Cal coverage for eligible low-income pregnant Californians while their full Medi-Cal application is pending.

title: Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP)
text: Pregnancy coverage option for people who meet Medi-Cal Access Program requirements and have income above Medi-Cal limits.

title: Medi-Cal Reproductive Health
text: State overview of Medi-Cal reproductive health coverage, including contraception, abortion, STI care, and maternal health.

title: Medi-Cal All Plan Letter 24-003: Abortion Services
text: Guidance requiring Medi-Cal managed-care plans to cover abortion and related care, including rules on cost-sharing and utilization review.

title: Medi-Cal Eligibility Information Letter I 22-32: Abortion Services
text: Explains abortion coverage across Medi-Cal eligibility categories and presumptive pregnancy programs.

title: Family PACT
text: No-cost, confidential family planning and reproductive health services for eligible Californians, including contraceptive methods and supplies, emergency contraception, and education and counseling. Eligibility: California resident, family income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level, and no other insurance that covers family planning. Use the clinic finder on the website.

title: Medi-Cal Doula Services
text: Describes Medi-Cal coverage of doula support during pregnancy, birth, postpartum, miscarriage, and abortion, including how to access it and visit limits.

title: DMHC All Plan Letter 25-021: Infertility and Fertility Services (SB 729)
text: California guidance implementing SB 729 fertility coverage requirements. What a plan must cover depends on the plan type and market.

title: DMHC Spring 2026 Fertility Services Update
text: Summarizes California fertility coverage guidance and services that may be included, such as diagnostic testing, counseling, IVF, and egg or embryo freezing (cryopreservation).

title: Medicare Cervical and Vaginal Cancer Screenings
text: Details Medicare Part B coverage for Pap and HPV tests, pelvic exams, and clinical breast exams, under specified rules.

title: Medicare Mammograms
text: Explains Medicare Part B coverage for screening and diagnostic mammograms, including how often and what they cost.

title: Medi-Cal Transportation Services (NMT and NEMT)
text: Medi-Cal covers rides to and from covered appointments, including medical, dental, and mental health visits, and trips to pick up prescriptions and medical supplies. Non-Medical Transportation (car or public transit) is for people with full-scope Medi-Cal or who are pregnant, through the end of the month in which the 365th day postpartum falls. Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (wheelchair van, litter van, or ambulance) is for people who can't use a car or public transit and requires a prescription from a doctor. Managed-care members request rides from their plan's member services; fee-for-service members use the DHCS request form.

title: NKF Cares helpline
text: Free National Kidney Foundation helpline. Call 855-653-2273 or email nkfcares@kidney.org, in English and Spanish, Monday to Friday 9am to 7pm Eastern. It can also answer questions about pregnancy and kidney disease.

title: NKF Peers peer mentoring
text: Matches kidney patients, living donors, or care partners by phone with a trained mentor who has been through it themselves. Geared toward later-stage CKD.

title: Renal Support Network HOPEline
text: Confidential, toll-free peer support line run by people with kidney disease, open 10am to 6pm Pacific at 800-579-1970. Renal Support Network also runs in-person meetings and events in the Los Angeles area (Glendale).

title: Bay Area Association of Kidney Patients virtual support groups
text: Monthly support groups on Sundays over Zoom. Register through their calendar of events. Discussion leans toward stage 4 and beyond.

title: AAKP national support group directory
text: American Association of Kidney Patients directory of virtual and in-person kidney support groups by state.

title: AAKP California support group listings
text: AAKP's listings of in-person kidney support groups in California. These are maintained by hand, so check that a group is still meeting before you go.

title: NKF Online Communities
text: Free, anonymous online communities from the National Kidney Foundation, with separate groups for kidney disease, dialysis, transplant, kidney donors, and parents of children with kidney disease. The Kidney Disease community fits people in earlier stages best.

title: Mayo Clinic Connect: Chronic Kidney Disease group
text: Mayo Clinic's online community group where people with chronic kidney disease share experiences and questions.

title: Mayo Clinic Connect: Transplants group
text: Mayo Clinic's online community group for transplant recipients and candidates.

title: National Kidney Foundation
text: The National Kidney Foundation's site for patient education, programs, and support across all stages of kidney disease.

title: NKF: Pregnancy and Kidney Disease
text: Patient-education page on how kidney disease stage affects pregnancy risk. Women with mild kidney disease (stages 1-2), normal blood pressure, and little or no protein in the urine can often have a healthy pregnancy, while the risk of complications is much greater in stages 3-5. Also covers pregnancy after transplant, and notes that men on dialysis or with a transplant can father children.

title: UCLA Health Kidney Women's Health Program
text: A dedicated California program for women with kidney disease, with a multidisciplinary team spanning nephrology, maternal-fetal medicine, endocrinology, and cardiology.

title: Transplant Pregnancy Registry International (TPRI)
text: Run by the Gift of Life Institute. Provides information to transplant recipients thinking about having children after transplant, and to their healthcare providers. Check current contact details on TPRI's own site (some older pages list its former name, NTPR).

title: Medi-Cal Health Care Options (HCO): choosing or changing a Medi-Cal plan
text: New Medi-Cal members get a Choice Packet in the mail from Health Care Options (HCO). If you don't choose a plan within 30 days, Medi-Cal chooses one for you, and you get a confirmation letter and plan materials. Enroll by phone Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., at 1-800-430-4263 (TTY 1-800-430-7077), or online. People with a Medicare Advantage plan are automatically enrolled in the matching Medi-Cal plan when there is one. Some people may not have to join a Medi-Cal plan, including American Indians and Alaska Natives, people in foster care, adoption assistance, or Child Protective Services programs, residents of California Veterans Homes, and people with a medical exemption. Kaiser Permanente is a plan choice for people who were Kaiser members in the last 12 months, immediate family of a current member, current or former foster children, or people with both Medicare and Medi-Cal. PACE plans are for people 55 or older who need a higher level of care to live at home (see CalPACE.org). SCAN Health Plan, a Medicare Advantage Special Needs Plan covering Medicare and Medi-Cal benefits including transportation, is for people 65 or older with Medicare Parts A and B and Medi-Cal in Los Angeles, Riverside, San Bernardino, or San Diego County.

title: Chronic kidney disease: symptoms and causes
text: Mayo Clinic overview of CKD symptoms and causes, with plain-language context on risk factors, diagnosis, and when symptoms may appear.

title: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
text: National Kidney Foundation patient resource on CKD definition, kidney functions, stages, common symptoms, causes, testing, and treatment topics. Symptoms alone cannot diagnose CKD.

title: What Is Chronic Kidney Disease?
text: NIDDK overview of CKD, its definition, common causes and risk factors, tests used to diagnose it, and monitoring kidney function.

title: About Chronic Kidney Disease
text: CDC patient information about CKD, including risk factors, prevention, testing, and early detection.

title: Types of kidney disease
text: Kidney Care UK collection of patient information about different kidney diseases and living with kidney conditions.

title: Women's health risks and chronic kidney disease
text: DaVita patient education discussing women's health and CKD. Use for general context and distinguish it from peer-reviewed evidence or clinical guidance.

title: Women's Kidney Health in Focus: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
text: American Heart Association scientific statement on women's kidney health, including kidney and cardiovascular health across women's life stages. Treat as a scientific statement, not a clinical practice guideline.

title: Medications to avoid with chronic kidney disease
text: Fresenius Kidney Care patient education about medicines that may pose risks with CKD. Do not use this for individual medication decisions; verify against official labeling and the user's clinician or pharmacist.

title: Women's Health and Kidney Protective Medications
text: Review of sex-based differences in pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of kidney-protective medications and implications for women's health. It highlights underrepresentation of women in clinical trials and the need for sex-specific safety and efficacy analyses. Treat as a review, not an individualized medication recommendation.

title: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI)
text: National Kidney Foundation overview of AKI, a sudden loss of kidney filtering function over hours or days, possible symptoms, causes, testing, and treatment. Symptoms vary, and some people have no obvious symptoms.

title: Kidney failure: symptoms and causes
text: Mayo Clinic patient overview of kidney failure symptoms and causes. Use for general education; symptoms alone do not establish a diagnosis.

title: Glomerular diseases
text: Cleveland Clinic overview of glomerular diseases, conditions affecting the kidney's filtering units, with general information about causes, signs, and evaluation.

title: Glomerular Disease
text: NIDDK information about glomerular diseases, how glomerular damage affects kidney filtering, signs such as blood or protein in urine, and evaluation.

title: Kidney infection (pyelonephritis)
text: Cleveland Clinic patient overview of kidney infection, symptoms, causes, diagnosis, and treatment. Fever, flank pain, or feeling very unwell can warrant prompt clinical assessment.

title: Kidney Infection (Pyelonephritis)
text: NIDDK patient information about kidney infections, including causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

title: Pregnancy, fertility, and babies after kidney transplant
text: National Kidney Foundation patient resource about fertility and pregnancy after kidney transplant. Encourage planning with transplant and obstetric care teams; this is not individualized preconception advice.

title: Menopause and kidney disease
text: Kidney Care UK patient information about menopause and kidney disease, including symptoms and questions to discuss with a kidney care team.

title: Medicines during pregnancy
text: Mayo Clinic patient information about medicine use during pregnancy. For kidney disease or transplant medication questions, direct the user to their nephrologist, obstetric clinician, and pharmacist; do not advise starting or stopping a medicine.
